title: Retrospective comparison of neoadjuvant FLOT versus CROSS treatment strategies in patients with esophageal and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma
summary:
This retrospective study analyzes clinical data from patients with esophageal cancer or cancer of the gastroesophageal junction treated at the University Hospital Bonn.

The aim is to compare two established neoadjuvant treatment strategies (FLOT and CROSS). The primary endpoint is pathological complete response, defined as the absence of residual tumor in the surgical specimen after treatment.

Secondary endpoints include surgical outcomes, tumor response, postoperative complications, 90-day mortality, and overall survival.

Only existing routine clinical data are analyzed. No additional examinations or interventions are performed.

interventions.name: Patients treated with neoadjuvant perioperative chemotherapy according to the FLOT regimen.
Patients treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy according to the CROSS protocol.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adenocarcinoma and/or squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus or the gastroesophageal junction (Siewert types I–III)
Neoadjuvant treatment intention with either CROSS or FLOT
Surgical resection performed at the study center
Availability of complete clinical and pathological data
Exclusion criteria:
Other histological tumor types
No neoadjuvant treatment setting
Prior treatment with alternative therapeutic regimens
